test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct group of fundamental rights provided by the Constitution of India from the given alternatives.

A. Right to equality

B. Right to freedom of religion

C. Right to financial support for higher and professional education

D. Right to constitutional remedies

E. Right to paternal properties
solution:
The correct answer is __**A, B and D**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct group of fundamental rights** provided by the Constitution is:
 
• **A. Right to equality**
 
• **B. Right to freedom of religion**
 
• **D. Right to constitutional remedies**
 
• These rights are fundamental to safeguarding individual liberty and equality in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A. Right to Equality**

 
 
• This is a fundamental right guaranteed under **Articles 14 to 18** of the Constitution. It includes:
 
• **Equality before the law** (Article 14).
 
• **Prohibition of discrimination** on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth (Article 15).
 
• **Equality of opportunity in public employment** (Article 16).
 
• **Abolition of untouchability** (Article 17).
 
• **Abolition of titles** (Article 18).
 
 
 
• **B. Right to Freedom of Religion**
 
 
• Guaranteed under **Articles 25 to 28**, this fundamental right ensures:
 
• **Freedom of conscience** and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion (Article 25).
 
• Freedom to manage religious affairs (Article 26).
 
• Freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any religion (Article 27).
 
• Freedom in attending religious instruction in educational institutions (Article 28).
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• This is a crucial fundamental right under **Article 32**.
 
• It empowers individuals to approach the Supreme Court or High Courts to enforce other fundamental rights if they are violated.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described this as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.
 
• Remedies include writs such as **habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto**.
